slice: Finance commercial subroute polish: Vendors, Billing/Tax, Leave/Time
intent: Continue the Bominal-grade cohesive Oyatie dashboard by upgrading sparse finance subroutes into interactive FD-001 product workload and Oyatie Cloud substrate proof surfaces with SSR parity.
product_direction: Oyatie will build a hyperscaler-grade cloud substrate and dogfood all FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads on that substrate. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the substrate that proves the platform can host real production tenants.
implementation_summary: Added dynamic and SSR-static finance anchor boards for Vendors & spend, Billing & tax, and Leave & time.
Each board carries FD-001 workload framing, Oyatie Cloud tenant/substrate proof framing, local-only/no-mutation boundaries, three proof cards, status text, and 10 interactive finance anchor actions.

Added fallback JS interactions for finance anchor actions, including routes to ledger/vendors/billing/leave, Workflow, Oyatie Cloud FinOps, policy, audit ledger, evidence spine, Mail, Messenger, and Community without backend mutation.
Added responsive finance anchor CSS matching the existing workforce/onboarding/identity proof-card design system.

visual_verdict.category_match: Cohesive product dashboard finance subroutes with Bominal-grade dense controls
visual_verdict.reasoning: The prior sparse finance panels now have consistent proof-card density, explicit FD-001/Oyatie Cloud framing, local-only boundaries, and visually functional routes into policy, evidence, and built-in communications. The cards inherit existing product design tokens instead of creating a separate visual language.
differences: The panels are still a prototype and are intentionally not wired to real banking, payroll, tax, billing, vendor, HRIS, or cloud backends.
Pixel diffs primarily reflect added content height and new proof cards rather than unintended layout drift.
suggestions: Continue applying this anchor-board pattern to any remaining sparse subroutes until the full dashboard is uniformly dense.
Consider a future route-state helper shared across shell and fallback scopes once the Oya VCS slice permits deeper JS consolidation.
